speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues; to begin, have you experienced any trauma to this knee recently, or did the swelling develop spontaneously?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (JIA) with a familial predisposition.

Given the spontaneous onset in an 18-month-old with a family history, we need to rule out septic arthritis and assess for joint inflammation. REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP, and Rheumatoid Factor. REQUEST IMAGES: Right Knee X-Ray.
